answer: A reef of agents can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that decays with inactivity, like pigment fading from a shell left in the sun. New identities start with zero trust and must earn reputation through verified, useful work over time; a whisper of activity buys nothing. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital and sustained effort per identity, while honest agents keep their stake and history, making mass fakery unprofitable.
